title: Leaving Henderson before the Little Brown Jug tour
summary: Babe reminds Joe that he left before the tour. Thomas explains the football-game bookings, Dance mentions Sid Catlett, and Joe left in 1936 as the band headed west.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Well, what happens then to Smack's band then, what happens to it. I mean it was going very successful at this time. Is this when he decides to work for Goodman or what happens?
I don't know. We had a little idea that didn't work out. I mean the guys in the band didn't work out. Huh, well, tell Stanley.
Scheduled to go on tour. We're getting ready to come out of the Terrace. At that time you left, that's when you left the band.
Well, I tell you what happened. You're right, Baby.
They had this tremendous tour booked.
Oh, yes. They had a thing booked for the Little Brown Jug game and all those kinds of things and ...
What do you mean the Brown Jug game?

Well, it's a football game, you know. And you play this, music is getting into the football idea. Like Mr. Langford give us allowance, years back, you don't have to be saluting, you dig it. And, Minnesota playing Northwestern, you learn the tunes and all that kind of things but those things are events in that part of the country. Glen Miller I think made the Little Brown Jug, you remember? Benx was a good buddy and he always had some things to help me on my writing.
Well, I was thinking that, yeah, you see when I came here first in '37, Smack was at the Savoy then and Sidney Cutlett Roy had gone and you had gone, Sidney Cappa. They had all gone.
Oh, Sid, I shouldn't have past him by. Well, '37 ...
You see you were with Christopher Columbus, etc., that's '36 and Walter Johnson replaces Cutlett Cappa in '36.
Yeah. Well, Sid Cutlett Cappa ... he was something else. he had an idea.
You left the band in '36, right?
When they were going on tour that's when you left the band.
